source.version: Saved arXiv 2507.21811v1 dated 29 Jul 2025 (cs.HC), marked 'Manuscript submitted to ACM'; the ACM Reference Format names ASSETS '25 and DOI 10.1145/3663547.3746384 (pp. 1-2). Complete saved markdown, including references and Appendices A-B, read; relevant pages independently checked in the 26-page PDF, including pp. 25-26, and Figure 7 inspected in memory. The publisher version was not independently read.
source.title_on_document: Helping or Homogenizing? GenAI as a Design Partner to Pre-Service SLPs for Just-in-Time Programming of AAC

supplement.where: Included in this PDF: Appendix A, with case studies on p. 25 and all four study images in Figure 8 on p. 26; Appendix B, the post-questionnaire, on p. 26. Separately, p. 12, Section 5 refers to external supplemental material containing all participant-configured VSDs; that collection is not reproduced in this PDF and was not read.
supplement.holds: The included appendices contain study images, hypothetical-user case studies, and questionnaire items. The separately mentioned external collection contains all VSDs configured in both conditions. No additional inferential statistics appear in the included appendices; the contents of the external collection beyond the paper's description are unverified.

paper_design_summary: Seventeen pre-service speech-language pathologists were recruited for an in-person within-person comparison of visual scene display (VSD) configuration with manual Snap Scene and a GPT-4o hotspot-suggestion prototype; application order and image allocation were counterbalanced, with randomization not stated (pp. 7-10, Sections 3.2.1 and 4-4.2.2). P5 was excluded, leaving 16 analyzed people and 64 VSDs, with 32 VSDs per condition (p. 12, Section 5; p. 20, Section 8). The paper assessed creation time, confidence, hotspot counts, three best-practice quality measures, hotspot content and communication functions, and homogeneity using each hotspot set's embedding against the average across both conditions; Sections 4.4.2 and 5.3.2 call this cosine similarity, but Figure 7 labels it 'Divergence' and interprets the lower prototype value as greater homogeneity, without specifying a conversion to cosine distance (pp. 11-16).

studies.label: Counterbalanced within-person experiment; randomization not stated (VSD configuration, Snap Scene vs genAI prototype)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two applications (Snap Scene vs genAI prototype) and which images were used with each; every participant used both
assignment.quote: The order of which application was used first and which images were used was counterbalanced across the entire experiment to mitigate any order effect.
assignment.locator: p. 10, Section 4.2.2; also p. 8, Section 4 ('The conditions were counterbalanced to address ordering effects')

arms.name: Prototype (genAI hotspot suggestions)
arms.description: Web app on a tablet; GPT-4o generates a ranked list of hotspots for the uploaded image, which the participant can use, edit, delete, or add to

arms.name: Snap Scene (control)
arms.description: Tobii Dynavox's Snap Scene, a commercial VSD app with no AI suggestions; participant creates hotspots manually

participants.exclusions: 17 recruited and participated (p. 8, Section 4.1; p. 9, Table 1). P5's data were removed because of an application error with the control software (p. 12, Section 5), leaving 16; 64 VSDs = 16 x 4 (32 per condition). The paper gives no count at assignment and does not say that order was randomized, so n_randomized is null.
participants.who: Pre-service speech-language pathologists (undergraduate and graduate students in communication sciences and disorders with some clinical experience) at a large R1 university, recruited by convenience sampling
participants.quote: We recruited seventeen pre-service speech-language pathologists (SLPs) from a large R1 university in the United States.
participants.locator: p. 8, Section 4.1; p. 12, Section 5 (P5 removed); abstract p. 2 states N=16

ai_tool.name_model: OpenAI GPT-4o via public API (multimodal), inside a ReactJS web prototype
ai_tool.how_used: On image upload, GPT-4o returns suggested hotspots (words or phrases) shown in a list; participants use, edit, delete, or add hotspots and draw them on the image (pp. 6-8, Sections 3.2-3.3)

task.description: Configure visual scene displays: choose and label hotspots (communication options) on a photo for a hypothetical minimally verbal child described in a case study; two images (play and retelling a past activity) per application
task.duration: not_stated; median time per VSD 77 s (Snap Scene) and 63.5 s (prototype), p. 12

outcomes.name: Homogeneity of VSD hotspot sets (reported cosine similarity; Figure 7 labels divergence)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Each VSD's set of hotspots was embedded with SentenceTransformers using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and compared with the average embedding across both conditions. There were 64 VSDs, 32 per condition, from the same 16 analyzed people. AI suggestions were available during prototype configuration; Snap Scene was manual. The text calls the metric cosine similarity, while Figure 7 calls it divergence and the authors interpret lower prototype values as greater homogeneity. The recorded direction follows the authors' interpretation of lower diversity; the transformation is unresolved (p. 12, Section 4.4.2 and Section 5; p. 15, Section 5.3.2; p. 16, Figure 7).

contrasts.reported: Prototype mean = 0.39 ± 0.09 vs Snap Scene mean = 0.46 ± 0.07; t(31) = 3.4037, p < 0.05, d = 0.60, 95% CI[0.26, 1.02], reported as higher homogeneity for VSDs configured using the prototype. The quantities following ± are not labeled, and the standardizer for d is not specified. Sections 4.4.2 and 5.3.2 call the calculation cosine similarity to the average embedding across both conditions; Figure 7 labels the axis 'Divergence'. No conversion to cosine distance is specified.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 4.4.2 and opening of Section 5; p. 15, Section 5.3.2; p. 16, Figure 7.

diversity_detail.metric: Reported cosine similarity of each VSD's hotspot-set embedding to the pooled average embedding; Figure 7 instead labels the axis 'Divergence'. The authors interpret lower prototype values as greater homogeneity. No distance transformation is specified.
diversity_detail.embedding_model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2, using the Python SentenceTransformers library (p. 12, Section 4.4.2).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each VSD hotspot set compared with the average embedding across BOTH conditions, rather than separate condition centroids; 64 VSDs, 32 per condition, contributed by the same 16 people (p. 12, Section 4.4.2 and Section 5; p. 20, Section 8).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Printed t(31) = 3.4037, p < 0.05; d = 0.60, 95% CI[0.26, 1.02] (p. 15, Section 5.3.2). The paper does not describe pairing, adjustment for repeated outputs from each participant, or the standardizer for d; the quantities following ± are not labeled.
diversity_detail.notes: The unit is a VSD hotspot set, not an independent person. Similarity/divergence terminology and interpretation remain unresolved; the paper's t-test and interval must not be assumed to reflect participant-level precision.

outcomes.name: Share of unique hotspots
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Reported unique-hotspot count divided by the total hotspot count in each condition-level pool. The two pools contain 94 Snap Scene hotspots and 153 prototype hotspots; these are aggregate output counts and percentages, not people or participant-level scores. No procedure for identifying unique hotspots is specified (p. 15, Section 5.3.3).

contrasts.reported: Snap Scene: 51 of 94 hotspots unique (54.26%); prototype: 56 of 153 hotspots unique (36.60%); both conditions: 84 of 247 unique (34.01%). No test reported.

diversity_detail.metric: Proportion of unique hotspots: reported unique-hotspot count divided by the total hotspot count in each pool.
diversity_detail.embedding_model: not_stated; no embedding model is specified for the unique-hotspot count.
diversity_detail.computed_over: Two condition-level pools: Snap Scene 51/94 unique hotspots (54.26%) and prototype 56/153 (36.60%). The combined pool is additionally reported as 84/247 (34.01%); it is not a third condition (p. 15, Section 5.3.3).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Descriptive aggregate counts and percentages only; no test or interval is reported (p. 15, Section 5.3.3).
diversity_detail.notes: The unit is the condition-level set of hotspots. The procedure for identifying unique hotspots is not specified. These hotspot counts do not count people, and the prototype has a lower unique proportion but a higher absolute unique count.

outcomes.name: VSD quality: hotspots focused on the people, activities, or social interactions in the scene (quality measure 2)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Quality measure 2: share of final hotspots focused on people, activities, or social interactions in the scene. The output unit is a hotspot; there are 247 final hotspots, 94 from Snap Scene and 153 from the prototype. This is an output-coded descriptive share, not a self-report rating (p. 12, Section 4.4.2 and Section 5; pp. 13-14, Section 5.1.4).

contrasts.reported: Snap Scene: 95.74% of hotspots focused on the people, activities, or social interactions in the scene; prototype: 84.97%. The hotspot pools contain 94 and 153 hotspots, respectively. No inferential test or interval reported.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 4.4.2 and opening of Section 5; pp. 13-14, Section 5.1.4.

outcomes.name: VSD quality: share of VSDs using 2–4 hotspots (quality measure 1)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Quality measure 1: whether each VSD uses 2–4 hotspots, a best-practice recommendation intended to avoid excessive visual stimulation and overlapping hotspots. The unit is a VSD; 64 VSDs were analyzed, 32 per condition. The reported 60.50% is retained exactly, without recalculation or inferred numerators (p. 12, Section 4.4.2 and Section 5; p. 13, Section 5.1.4).

contrasts.reported: Snap Scene: 60.50% of VSDs used between 2 and 4 hotspots; prototype: 40.63%. There were 32 VSDs per condition. No inferential test or interval reported; 60.50% is recorded exactly as printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 4.4.2 and opening of Section 5; p. 13, Section 5.1.4.

outcomes.name: VSD quality: share of single-word hotspots (quality measure 3)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Quality measure 3: developmental appropriateness operationalized as the proportion of final hotspots containing a single word. The unit is a hotspot; 247 final hotspots were analyzed, 94 from Snap Scene and 153 from the prototype (p. 12, Section 4.4.2 and Section 5; p. 14, Section 5.1.4).

contrasts.reported: Snap Scene: single-word hotspots 78.70% of the time; prototype: 91.50%. The hotspot pools contain 94 and 153 hotspots, respectively. No inferential test or interval reported.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 4.4.2 and opening of Section 5; p. 14, Section 5.1.4.

outcomes.name: Number of hotspots per VSD
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of final hotspots in each configured VSD. The comparison includes 64 VSDs, 32 per condition, from the same 16 analyzed people. The n=94 and n=153 printed in Section 5.1.3 are total hotspot counts, not people. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test is reported, but the paper does not describe how pairs were formed or how repeated VSDs from each participant were handled (p. 12, Section 5; p. 13, Section 5.1.3; p. 20, Section 8).

contrasts.reported: Median hotspots per VSD: Snap Scene 3; prototype 5. Wilcoxon signed-rank W = 5.5, Z = −4.5567, p < 0.05; r = 0.57. The reported n=94 (Snap Scene) and n=153 (prototype) count hotspots; there are 32 VSDs per condition.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 12, opening of Section 5; p. 13, Section 5.1.3; p. 14, Figure 5.

outcomes.name: Communication-function quality: share of hotspots supporting social closeness
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two researchers coded final hotspots using Light's Functions of Communication framework, with an additional Other category; Cohen's kappa was 0.66. The focal quality measure is the share supporting social closeness, which the discussion identifies as an important VSD function; the other category shares describe the communication-function distribution. The unit is a hotspot, with 247 final hotspots, 94 from Snap Scene and 153 from the prototype. These are coded output shares, not self-reports (pp. 11-12, Section 4.4.1; p. 12, Section 5; pp. 15-16, Section 5.3.4 and Table 3; p. 18, Section 6.2.1).

contrasts.reported: Table 3, Snap Scene vs prototype: Social Closeness 5.3% vs 0.7%; Information Transfer 93.6% vs 98.7%; Expressing Wants & Needs 0.0% vs 0.0%; Social Etiquette 0.0% vs 0.0%; Other 1.1% vs 0.7%. These descriptive shares use the 94 vs 153 final-hotspot pools. No inferential test or interval reported. Direction refers to the social-closeness share.
contrasts.locator: PDF pp. 11-12, Section 4.4.1; p. 12, opening of Section 5; pp. 15-16, Section 5.3.4 and Table 3; p. 18, Section 6.2.1.

eligibility.reason: Counterbalanced within-person experiment; randomization not stated (pp. 8 and 10, Sections 4 and 4.2.2). Seventeen people were recruited and P5 was excluded for a control-software application error, leaving 16 analyzed people, below 50 (p. 8, Section 4.1; p. 12, Section 5; p. 20, Section 8). The same people completed both conditions. Output-based diversity and quality are measured (p. 12, Section 4.4.2; pp. 13-16, Sections 5.1.4 and 5.3.2-5.3.4), meeting criterion 3. Core eligibility is no on sample size. The complete text, including Appendices A-B, does not establish either random or explicitly non-random allocation; context_class remains provisionally none rather than assuming an observational design.

one_line_finding: With 16 analyzed pre-service SLPs, the authors report greater homogeneity with GPT-4o hotspot suggestions than with Snap Scene (0.39 ± 0.09 vs 0.46 ± 0.07; t(31) = 3.4037, d = 0.60; p. 15, Section 5.3.2, with unresolved cosine-similarity/divergence terminology in Figure 7 on p. 16) and a lower proportion of unique hotspots (56/153, 36.60%, vs 51/94, 54.26%; p. 15, Section 5.3.3).

applied.old: With 16 pre-service SLPs, VSDs configured with GPT-4o hotspot suggestions were more homogeneous than those made with Snap Scene (divergence 0.39 ± 0.09 vs 0.46 ± 0.07, t(31) = 3.4037, d = 0.60; p. 15, Section 5.3.2) and had fewer unique hotspots (36.60% vs 54.26%; p. 15, Section 5.3.3).
applied.new: With 16 analyzed pre-service SLPs, the authors report greater homogeneity with GPT-4o hotspot suggestions than with Snap Scene (0.39 ± 0.09 vs 0.46 ± 0.07; t(31) = 3.4037, d = 0.60; p. 15, Section 5.3.2, with unresolved cosine-similarity/divergence terminology in Figure 7 on p. 16) and a lower proportion of unique hotspots (56/153, 36.60%, vs 51/94, 54.26%; p. 15, Section 5.3.3).
applied.quote: In the Snap Scene condition 51 of 94 hotspots were unique (54.26%). In the prototype condition 56 of 153 hotspots were unique (36.60%).
